hints.title: First-Child Next-Sibling Isomorphism
hints.text: Any general multi-way branching tree maps bijectively into a standard binary tree by linking the primary child to the left branch and subsequent siblings along the right branch.

hints.title: Binary Pointer Direction Semantics
hints.text: A node left pointer references its first child. That child right pointer references its next sibling. Chains of right pointers encode sibling collections.

hints.title: Recursive Encoding and Decoding Blueprint
hints.text: Encode(root): b_root = TreeNode(root.val). If children exist, b_root.left = encode(children[0]). Iterate remaining children, chaining along right pointers. Decode(b_node): root = Node(b_node.val, []). Walk curr = b_node.left along right pointers, appending decode(curr) to children.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Visits each node once during transformation with recursion stack bounded by tree height.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Storing children as arbitrary subtrees without standard conventions loses sibling order relationships.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Left-child right-sibling encoding utilizes existing TreeNode pointer slots without auxiliary arrays.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Familiarity with the classic Knuth transform for representing multi-way trees as binary trees.

solutions.approach: Java Binary Tree Sibling Pointer Encoding
